skills.name: Minimize
skills.shortExplanation: Hide the window into the bottom taskbar without closing your work.
skills.simulatorControl: Top right window control button (-) or taskbar button.

lessonSections.title: Meet Minimize
lessonSections.teacherText: The Minimize button is shaped like a small minus sign (➖) in the top-right corner of your window. When you click it, your window hides down into the taskbar.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Point to the top-right corner of your screen. Ask students: 'What shape looks like a takeaway line or minus sign?'
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Look at the top-right corner of the window. Notice the minus sign (➖) button.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Ready to find the button!

lessonSections.title: Find the Button
lessonSections.teacherText: Help students locate the Minimize button. The button is highlighted on screen.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask students: 'Can you find the highlighted minus button in the top-right corner?'
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click the highlighted Minimize button (➖) in the top-right corner.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Great job! You found the Minimize button!

lessonSections.title: Watch It Work
lessonSections.teacherText: When Minimize is clicked, the browser window slides down into the taskbar at the bottom of the screen. Your work is kept safe!
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Explain to students: 'Minimizing does not delete or close your work. It just puts Chrome away until you need it again.'
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Watch the presentation screen to see how Chrome slides down into the taskbar.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Now you are ready to try it yourself!

lessonSections.title: Guided Practice — Minimize
lessonSections.teacherText: Direct students to click the Minimize button on their screen. Their window will slide down into the taskbar.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Instruct students: 'Click the Minimize button in the top-right corner of your Chrome window.'
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click the Minimize button (➖) to hide Chrome into the taskbar.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Awesome! Chrome is now minimized in your taskbar!

lessonSections.title: Guided Practice — Bring It Back
lessonSections.teacherText: Direct students to click the Chrome icon on their taskbar to bring the window back.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Instruct students: 'Look at the bottom taskbar. Click the Chrome icon to open your window again.'
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click the Chrome icon on the bottom taskbar to restore your window.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Nice work! You brought Chrome back onto the screen!

lessonSections.title: Independent Challenge
lessonSections.teacherText: Students must minimize Chrome and then restore it from the taskbar without visual highlights.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Tell students: 'Show that you can minimize Chrome to the taskbar, then open it back up without help.'
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Hide Chrome into the taskbar, then bring it back!
lessonSections.completionMessage: Outstanding! You mastered minimizing and restoring Chrome!
intermediateMessages: Great! Now click the Chrome taskbar button to bring it back.

lessonSections.title: Minimize or Close?
lessonSections.teacherText: Review the difference between Minimize (hides window) and Close (shuts window).
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask the class: 'Which button hides a window into the taskbar without closing your work?'
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Which button hides a window into the taskbar but keeps your work open?
lessonSections.completionMessage: Correct! Minimize hides your window without closing your work.

choices.label: Close
choices.feedback: Close shuts the window completely. Try Minimize!

lessonSections.title: Lesson Complete
lessonSections.teacherText: Celebrate student success! Reinforce that Minimize hides a window without closing it.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Congratulate students on completing their first Chrome browser skill lesson!
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Minimize hides a window without closing it. Excellent job!
lessonSections.completionMessage: Lesson Complete! You are a Minimize master!

skills.name: Maximize & Restore
skills.shortExplanation: Make a window fill the desktop, then return it to its smaller size.
skills.simulatorControl: The square Maximize button changes into Restore Down when the window fills the desktop.

lessonSections.title: Meet Maximize
lessonSections.teacherText: The Maximize button looks like a square in the top-right corner. It makes a window grow to fill the available desktop.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Point to the square beside Minimize. Ask: “Which button looks like one large window?”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Look for the square button in the top-right corner of the Chrome window.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Ready to find Maximize!

lessonSections.title: Find the Button
lessonSections.teacherText: Help students locate the square Maximize button between Minimize and Close.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask: “Can you find the highlighted square button?”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click the highlighted square Maximize button.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Great job! You found the Maximize button!

lessonSections.title: Watch It Work
lessonSections.teacherText: Maximize makes Chrome fill the desktop. The same button then changes into Restore Down, which returns Chrome to its smaller size.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Point out how the square icon changes after Chrome becomes maximized.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Watch Maximize fill the desktop, then watch Restore Down return the window to its smaller size.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Now you are ready to try it!

lessonSections.title: Guided Practice — Maximize
lessonSections.teacherText: Students click Maximize to make Chrome fill the available desktop.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Say: “Click the square Maximize button.”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click the square Maximize button to make Chrome fill the desktop.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Excellent! Chrome now fills the desktop!

lessonSections.title: Guided Practice — Restore Down
lessonSections.teacherText: When Chrome is maximized, the button changes to Restore Down. Clicking it returns the window to its previous size.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Say: “Click Restore Down to make Chrome a smaller window again.”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click the Restore Down button to return Chrome to its smaller size.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Nice work! Chrome is a smaller window again!

lessonSections.title: Independent Challenge
lessonSections.teacherText: Students maximize Chrome and then restore it down without visual highlights.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Say: “Make Chrome fill the desktop, then return it to a smaller window.”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Make Chrome fill the desktop, then return it to its smaller size.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Outstanding! You mastered Maximize and Restore Down!
intermediateMessages: Great! Now click Restore Down to make the window smaller again.

lessonSections.title: Maximize or Minimize?
lessonSections.teacherText: Review that Maximize fills the desktop while Minimize hides the window in the taskbar.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask: “Which button makes a window fill the desktop?”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Which button makes a window grow to fill the desktop?
lessonSections.completionMessage: Correct! Maximize makes the window fill the desktop.

choices.label: Minimize
choices.feedback: Minimize hides the window. Try Maximize!

lessonSections.title: Lesson Complete
lessonSections.teacherText: Celebrate success and reinforce that Maximize fills the available desktop.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Congratulate students on learning Maximize and Restore Down.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Maximize makes a window fill the desktop. Excellent job!
lessonSections.completionMessage: Lesson Complete! You are a Maximize master!

skills.name: Close & Reopen
skills.shortExplanation: Close the Chrome window, then open a fresh window from the taskbar.
skills.simulatorControl: Top right window red/hover button (X) or taskbar button to re-open.

lessonSections.title: Meet Close
lessonSections.teacherText: The Close button is the X in the top-right corner. It shuts the window instead of merely hiding it.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask: “Which symbol usually means stop, remove, or close?”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Look for the X button in the top-right corner of Chrome.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Ready to find Close!

lessonSections.title: Find the Button
lessonSections.teacherText: Help students locate the X at the far-right side of the window controls.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask: “Can you find the highlighted X?”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click the highlighted X button.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Great job! You found the Close button!

lessonSections.title: Watch It Work
lessonSections.teacherText: Close removes the window from the desktop. Clicking Chrome on the taskbar opens a fresh window.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Remind students that Close is different from Minimize and may end unfinished work on some pages.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Watch the X close Chrome, then watch the taskbar open a fresh window.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Now you are ready to try it!

lessonSections.title: Guided Practice — Close
lessonSections.teacherText: Students click the X to close their simulated Chrome window.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Say: “Click the X in the top-right corner.”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click the X to close Chrome.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You closed the Chrome window!

lessonSections.title: Guided Practice — Reopen
lessonSections.teacherText: Students click Chrome on the taskbar to open a fresh window.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Say: “Find Chrome on the taskbar and click it.”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click Chrome on the taskbar to open a fresh window.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Nice work! You opened a fresh Chrome window!

lessonSections.title: Independent Challenge
lessonSections.teacherText: Students close Chrome and reopen it without highlights.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Say: “Close Chrome completely, then open a fresh Chrome window.”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Close Chrome, then open it again from the taskbar.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Outstanding! You closed and reopened Chrome!
intermediateMessages: Chrome is closed. Now click it on the taskbar to open it again.

lessonSections.title: Close or Minimize?
lessonSections.teacherText: Review that Close shuts the window while Minimize keeps it open in the taskbar.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask: “Which button shuts the window instead of hiding it?”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Which button shuts the Chrome window?
lessonSections.completionMessage: Correct! Close shuts the window.

choices.label: Minimize
choices.feedback: Minimize hides the window but keeps it open. Try Close!

lessonSections.title: Lesson Complete
lessonSections.teacherText: Celebrate success and reinforce the difference between Close and Minimize.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Congratulate students on learning to close and reopen Chrome.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Close shuts a window. Chrome can be opened again from the taskbar.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Lesson Complete! You mastered Close and Reopen!

skills.name: Back & Forward
skills.shortExplanation: Move to a page you visited before, then move forward again.
skills.simulatorControl: The left and right arrow buttons beside the address bar.

lessonSections.title: Meet Back & Forward
lessonSections.teacherText: Back returns to a page you visited earlier. Forward revisits a page after you have used Back.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Compare the arrows to walking backward and forward along the same path.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Look for the left Back arrow and right Forward arrow beside the address bar.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Ready to find Back!

lessonSections.title: Find Back
lessonSections.teacherText: Back is the arrow pointing left near the upper-left side of Chrome.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask: “Which arrow points toward where we were before?”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click the highlighted Back arrow.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Great job! You found the Back button!

lessonSections.title: Watch It Work
lessonSections.teacherText: Back returns from Today’s Story to Reading Corner. Forward then revisits Today’s Story.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Point out that Forward becomes useful after Back has been used.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Watch Back return to the previous page, then watch Forward revisit the page.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Now you are ready to try!

lessonSections.title: Guided Practice — Back
lessonSections.teacherText: Students are on Today’s Story and use Back to return to Reading Corner.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Say: “Click Back to return to the page you just visited.”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click Back to return from Today’s Story to Reading Corner.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Excellent! You returned to Reading Corner!

lessonSections.title: Guided Practice — Forward
lessonSections.teacherText: Students have returned to Reading Corner and use Forward to revisit Today’s Story.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Say: “Now click Forward to revisit the story.”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click Forward to revisit Today’s Story.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Nice work! You moved forward to Today’s Story!

lessonSections.title: Independent Challenge
lessonSections.teacherText: Students move back to Reading Corner and forward to Today’s Story without highlights.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Say: “Go back one page, then move forward again.”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Go back to Reading Corner, then forward to Today’s Story.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Outstanding! You mastered Back and Forward!
intermediateMessages: Great! Now click Forward to revisit Today’s Story.

lessonSections.title: Back or Reload?
lessonSections.teacherText: Back returns to an earlier page. Reload refreshes the page currently displayed.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask: “Which button returns to the page we just left?”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Which button returns to the page you visited before?
lessonSections.completionMessage: Correct! Back returns to the previous page.

choices.label: Reload
choices.feedback: Reload refreshes the current page. Try Back!

lessonSections.title: Lesson Complete
lessonSections.teacherText: Celebrate success and reinforce how browsing history controls both arrows.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Congratulate students on moving through pages safely.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Back returns to an earlier page. Forward revisits the page after using Back.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Lesson Complete! You mastered Back and Forward!

skills.name: Reload
skills.shortExplanation: Refresh the current web page to get the latest updates.
skills.simulatorControl: Circular arrow button next to Forward.

lessonSections.title: Meet Reload
lessonSections.teacherText: Introduce the circular arrow. Reload loads the current page again; it does not go Back or Forward.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Trace a circle with your finger and say: “Reload refreshes this page.”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Find the circular arrow near the address bar. Reload refreshes the page you are viewing.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Ready for the next step.

lessonSections.title: Find the Reload Button
lessonSections.teacherText: Let students identify Reload before using it.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask: “Which arrow goes around in a circle?”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click the circular Reload arrow.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You found Reload!

lessonSections.title: Watch Reload Work
lessonSections.teacherText: Model refreshing the noticeboard. Point out the unchanged address and the updated message.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Say: “We are still on the Class Noticeboard. We loaded it again.”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Watch the cursor click Reload. The notice updates, but the address stays the same.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Ready for the next step.

lessonSections.title: Refresh the Noticeboard
lessonSections.teacherText: Students refresh the current noticeboard page.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask students to click once, then look for the updated message.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click Reload once to see the latest class message.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You refreshed the noticeboard and stayed on the same page!

lessonSections.title: Same Page, Another Refresh
lessonSections.teacherText: Two refreshes demonstrate that reloading does not move through browser history.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Point to the address before and after each refresh. Explain that a real page might not visibly change.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Reload once. Check the address, then reload again. Are you still on the same page?
lessonSections.completionMessage: Two refreshes, and the address stayed the same!
intermediateMessages: One refresh! Check the address, then reload once more.

lessonSections.title: Reload Challenge
lessonSections.teacherText: Students choose Reload without a highlight.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask: “How can you refresh this page while staying here?”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Refresh the Class Noticeboard without using Back or Forward.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You chose Reload to refresh the current page!

lessonSections.title: Reload or Back?
lessonSections.teacherText: Check that students distinguish refreshing from returning to a previous page.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask students to explain their choice.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Which button refreshes the page you are viewing?
lessonSections.completionMessage: Correct! Reload refreshes the current page.

choices.label: Back
choices.feedback: Back returns to a previous page. Try Reload to refresh this page.

lessonSections.title: Reload Complete
lessonSections.teacherText: Review the difference between Reload and Back/Forward.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask: “Does Reload take us to a different page?”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Reload refreshes the current page. Back and Forward move between pages you have visited.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Ready for the next step.

skills.description: Refresh the current page without going Back or Forward.
skills.shortDescription: Refresh the current page without going Back or Forward.

skills.name: Home
skills.shortExplanation: Instantly return to your main school home page.
skills.simulatorControl: House icon on the navigation bar.

lessonSections.title: Meet the Button
lessonSections.placeholderDescription: Find the house-shaped Home button.

lessonSections.title: Watch It Work
lessonSections.placeholderDescription: Observe how Home jumps straight to your starting page.

lessonSections.title: Guided Practice
lessonSections.placeholderDescription: Click the Home button to jump back to the main portal.

lessonSections.title: Student Challenge
lessonSections.placeholderDescription: Navigate away and use Home to quickly return.

skills.name: Using the Address Bar
skills.shortExplanation: Use the Address Bar to visit a website or search for information.
skills.simulatorControl: Long text box near the top of Chrome.

lessonSections.title: Meet the Address Bar
lessonSections.teacherText: The Address Bar is the long box near the top of Chrome. It can take you directly to a website or search for information.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Point to the Address Bar and say: “This box has two jobs: go to a website or search.”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: The Address Bar is the long box near the top of Chrome. You can type a website or a search here.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Ready to find the Address Bar!

lessonSections.title: Find the Address Bar
lessonSections.teacherText: Students identify the long Address Bar before typing into it.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask: “Where would you click before typing a website?”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click the highlighted Address Bar.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You found the Address Bar!

lessonSections.title: Watch: Click, Type, Enter
lessonSections.teacherText: Model the three-step routine: click the Address Bar, type nasa.gov, then press Enter.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Have students repeat: “Click, Type, Enter.”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Watch the cursor click the Address Bar, type nasa.gov, and press Enter.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Now you are ready to try!

lessonSections.title: Go to a Website
lessonSections.teacherText: Students use the Address Bar to go directly to the simulated NASA website.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Say: “Click the Address Bar, type nasa.gov, then press Enter.”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click the Address Bar. Type nasa.gov. Press Enter.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Excellent! You used a web address to go directly to NASA!

lessonSections.title: Search with the Address Bar
lessonSections.teacherText: The Address Bar can also search. Students type words instead of a website address.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Say: “This time we are searching for a topic, not typing a website.”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click the Address Bar. Type ocean animals. Press Enter.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Great! You used the Address Bar to search!

lessonSections.title: Replace the Old Address
lessonSections.teacherText: Clicking the Address Bar selects the current address. Students can type something new without erasing it one letter at a time.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Point out the blue selection and say: “When it is selected, just start typing.”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: You are on NASA. Click the Address Bar, type space facts, and press Enter.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Nice work! You replaced the old address without backspacing through it!

lessonSections.title: Address Bar Challenge
lessonSections.teacherText: Students first visit nasa.gov, then use the same Address Bar to search for ocean animals without highlights.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Say: “Go to NASA. Then search for ocean animals.”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Go to nasa.gov. Then search for ocean animals.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Outstanding! You can use the Address Bar for websites and searches!
intermediateMessages: NASA opened! Now click the Address Bar and search for ocean animals.

lessonSections.title: Address Bar Complete
lessonSections.teacherText: Review the two jobs of the Address Bar: go directly to a website or search for information.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Have students say the routine together: “Click, Type, Enter.”
lessonSections.studentInstruction: The Address Bar can open a website or search. Remember: Click, Type, Enter.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Lesson Complete! You mastered the Address Bar!

skills.description: Use the Address Bar to visit websites and search for information.
skills.shortDescription: Click, type, and press Enter to visit a website or search.

skills.name: New Tab
skills.shortExplanation: Open a fresh web page tab alongside your current page.
skills.simulatorControl: Plus (+) button next to the active tab.

lessonSections.title: Meet New Tab
lessonSections.teacherText: The plus button opens another tab. Your current page stays open.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Point to the plus beside the open tab.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: The plus button opens another tab. Your current page stays open.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You did it!

lessonSections.title: Find the Plus
lessonSections.teacherText: Click the plus button to show where New Tab is.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: This step identifies the button without opening a tab.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click the plus button to show where New Tab is.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You found New Tab!

lessonSections.title: Watch a New Tab Open
lessonSections.teacherText: Watch the cursor click plus. Notice that Reading Corner stays open.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Point out the original tab and the newly selected tab.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Watch the cursor click plus. Notice that Reading Corner stays open.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You did it!

lessonSections.title: Open Another Tab
lessonSections.teacherText: Click plus once to open a new tab.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask students to count the tabs afterward.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click plus once to open a new tab.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You opened another tab!

lessonSections.title: Your First Page Is Still There
lessonSections.teacherTitle: Your First Page Is Still There
lessonSections.teacherText: Click the Reading Corner tab to return to your first page.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Explain that opening a tab did not replace Reading Corner.
lessonSections.studentTitle: Your First Page Is Still There
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click the Reading Corner tab to return to your first page.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Reading Corner was still open!

lessonSections.title: New Tab Challenge
lessonSections.teacherText: Open a new tab, then switch back to Reading Corner.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Let students complete the two actions without highlights.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Open a new tab, then switch back to Reading Corner.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You opened another tab and returned to your first page!
intermediateMessages: New tab opened. Now choose Reading Corner.

lessonSections.title: Which Button Opens a Tab?
lessonSections.teacherText: Which button opens a new tab?
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask students to explain what the plus does.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Which button opens a new tab?
lessonSections.completionMessage: Correct! Plus opens a new tab.

choices.label: Tab X
choices.feedback: The small X closes a tab. Choose plus to open one.

lessonSections.title: New Tab Complete
lessonSections.teacherText: Plus opens another tab. Your other tabs stay open.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Have students explain what happened to their first page.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Plus opens another tab. Your other tabs stay open.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You did it!

skills.name: Switch Between Tabs
skills.shortExplanation: Choose another open tab while keeping your pages open.
skills.simulatorControl: Click the title of another open tab.

lessonSections.title: Meet Open Tabs
lessonSections.teacherText: Tabs let you keep several pages open. The active tab is the page you see.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Compare the active white tab with the other tab.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Tabs let you keep several pages open. The active tab is the page you see.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You did it!

lessonSections.title: Find Another Tab
lessonSections.teacherText: Click the Reading Corner tab title.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Identify the title area, away from its small X.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click the Reading Corner tab title.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You found another open tab!

lessonSections.title: Watch Tabs Switch
lessonSections.teacherText: Watch Reading Corner and Science Lab take turns being the active page.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Point out that neither tab closes.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Watch Reading Corner and Science Lab take turns being the active page.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You did it!

lessonSections.title: Choose Reading Corner
lessonSections.teacherText: Click Reading Corner to make it the active tab.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask which page is now visible.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click Reading Corner to make it the active tab.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Reading Corner is now active!

lessonSections.title: Switch Back to Science
lessonSections.teacherText: Click Science Lab to bring its page back.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Notice that the page remained open while another tab was active.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click Science Lab to bring its page back.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Science Lab was still open!

lessonSections.title: Three-Tab Challenge
lessonSections.teacherText: Choose Art Studio, then Reading Corner.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Let students find the correct titles without highlights.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Choose Art Studio, then Reading Corner.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You switched between the correct tabs!
intermediateMessages: Art Studio is active. Now choose Reading Corner.

lessonSections.title: Switch or Close?
lessonSections.teacherText: How do you see another open tab without closing it?
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Discuss why the title and the X do different things.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: How do you see another open tab without closing it?
lessonSections.completionMessage: Correct! Clicking the title switches tabs.

choices.label: Click its X
choices.feedback: The X closes a tab. Click its title to switch to it.

lessonSections.title: Switching Complete
lessonSections.teacherText: Click a tab title to see its page. Your other tabs stay open.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask a student to explain which tab is active.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click a tab title to see its page. Your other tabs stay open.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You did it!

skills.name: Close Tab
skills.shortExplanation: Close a specific open tab without closing the whole browser.
skills.simulatorControl: Small x icon on the right side of tab title.

lessonSections.title: Meet Close Tab
lessonSections.teacherText: The small X on a tab closes that tab. The window X is a different control.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Compare the small tab X with the window X in the far corner.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: The small X on a tab closes that tab. The window X is a different control.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You did it!

lessonSections.title: Find the Tab X
lessonSections.teacherText: Click the small X on the Science Lab tab.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: This identification step leaves the tab open.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Click the small X on the Science Lab tab.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You found the tab’s small X!

lessonSections.title: Watch One Tab Close
lessonSections.teacherText: Watch Science Lab close while Reading Corner stays open.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Point out that the Chrome window remains on the desktop.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Watch Science Lab close while Reading Corner stays open.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You did it!

lessonSections.title: Close Science Lab
lessonSections.teacherText: Close Science Lab using the small X on its tab.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Ask students which tab remains afterward.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Close Science Lab using the small X on its tab.
lessonSections.completionMessage: Science Lab closed. Reading Corner stayed open!

lessonSections.title: Keep the Page You Need
lessonSections.teacherText: Close Art Studio. Keep Reading Corner open.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Students choose the tab they are finished using.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Close Art Studio. Keep Reading Corner open.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You kept Reading Corner open!

lessonSections.title: Close Tab Challenge
lessonSections.teacherText: Close Art Studio, then Science Lab. Leave Reading Corner open.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Let students remove the two extra tabs without highlights.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Close Art Studio, then Science Lab. Leave Reading Corner open.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You closed the extra tabs and kept Reading Corner!
intermediateMessages: Art Studio closed. Now close Science Lab.

lessonSections.title: One Tab or Whole Window?
lessonSections.teacherText: Which control closes just one tab when several are open?
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Point to both kinds of X as you discuss the choices.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: Which control closes just one tab when several are open?
lessonSections.completionMessage: Correct! The small tab X closes that tab.

choices.label: Window X in the corner
choices.feedback: The window X closes the whole window. Choose the tab’s small X.

lessonSections.title: Close Tab Complete
lessonSections.teacherText: The small X closes a tab. Closing the last tab also closes the window.
lessonSections.teacherPrompt: Explain the last-tab exception and remind students to finish their work first.
lessonSections.studentInstruction: The small X closes a tab. Closing the last tab also closes the window.
lessonSections.completionMessage: You did it!
